name: Beera Chicken House
why_it_matters: Started in 1970 as a tiny stall by Beera; the tandoori chicken recipe finalised in 1972 hasn't changed. No artificial colour, just yogurt-and-spice marinade in a charcoal tandoor — the version Amritsaris correct outsiders about when they default to butter chicken.
insider_tip: Order half-tandoori with kaali dal, not butter chicken — the dal is what locals come back for. They run out of legs by 9pm; thigh pieces still available till close.
signature_address: Shop 100, Majitha Road, Opposite Bhandari Hospital, Bhawani Nagar, Amritsar 143001

name: Surjit Food Plaza
why_it_matters: Over four decades on Lawrence Road under owner Surjit Singh, who still works the floor most evenings. Tandoor seasoning leans Garam-Masala-and-Kashmiri-chilli; the kebabs are the consistent order, less so the gravy menu.
insider_tip: Lunch is quieter; dinner runs a 30-minute wait by 8pm. The mutton tikka is a sleeper — order it before the chicken to taste what the tandoor is doing properly.
signature_address: Nos 3-4, Ground Floor, Nehru Shopping Complex, Lawrence Road, Joshi Colony, Amritsar 143001

name: Makhan Fish and Chicken Corner
why_it_matters: S. Mohinder Singh inherited the Amritsari fish recipe from his father, opened the corner in March 1991 — but the family's been frying since 1962, hence the 'SINCE 1962' on the signboard. Fish marinated in salt for hours, dipped in besan batter, deep-fried to order.
insider_tip: Order the fish fry plain, not the curry — the besan crust is the entire point. Pair with garlic naan and a tandoori roti, skip the multi-cuisine pages.
signature_address: 21-A, Majitha Road, Sehaj Avenue, near Madaan Hospital, Amritsar 143001

name: Kanha Sweets
why_it_matters: Over fifty years on Lawrence Road, adjacent to Sandoz Hotel. The puri-chole is the breakfast Amritsaris drive across town for; small menu, AC seating section, no theatrics. The accompanying 'launji' — aloo pickle — is the stealth signature.
insider_tip: Puri chole stops at 5pm sharp — this is a breakfast-and-lunch shop, not a dinner one. Cash counter is faster than the seating queue if you're doing takeaway.
signature_address: Adjacent Sandoz Hotel, Lawrence Road, Amritsar 143001

name: Sanjha Chulha
area: Lawrence Road, opposite BBK DAV College
why_it_matters: AC kulcha specialist opposite BBK DAV College — flaky stuffed kulchas without the lane-side dust of the old-city joints. Generous portions, vegetarian-only, the safer-bet option for families staying at Lawrence Road hotels.
insider_tip: Order the aloo-pyaaz and butter-garlic kulcha as a pair — sharing one piece of each across two people is the move; both come buttered to the brink.
signature_address: Opposite BBK DAV College, Lawrence Road, Amritsar 143001

name: Novelty Sweets
why_it_matters: Founded in 1950 by S. Kartar Singh, then expanded by his son S. Bhupinder Singh into a Northern-India sweet brand. The Lawrence Road junction is now officially called Novelty Chowk because of this shop. Pure desi-ghee mithai, no shortcuts.
insider_tip: The pinni is the pack-and-fly buy — sealed boxes survive a 12-hour flight. Skip the freshly-fried jalebi here; that's a Gurdas Ram trip.
